solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Brand that's well-known without needing statement of quality

parts.note: ex is Latin for out of or without, as in ex-dividend

indicators.note: a statement is something spoken, so the word for quality is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: calibre is quality or standard of excellence

explanation.surface: A famous product brand so established it never needs to advertise how good it is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brand' looks like a trade name, but it is an old word for a sword; 'needing' is a link. EX plus a word sounding like CALIBRE gives the legendary blade.
explanation.definitionFit: Brand is a poetic word for a sword, and King Arthur's legendary blade is the most famous one of all.

clue.text: A number reportedly put away

indicators.note: reportedly means as said aloud, so the sound matters

parts.note: food that is put away is eaten, so ate

explanation.surface: A number of things are said to have been tidied away.
explanation.definitionFit: Eight is a number, the cardinal between seven and nine.

clue.text: Having spirit found in bars

definitions.meaning: a direction that appears in written music, which is divided into bars

explanation.walkthrough: 'bars' suggests pubs serving spirits, but they are measures of music.
explanation.definitionFit: Con brio is an Italian musical direction meaning with vigour, printed above bars of a score.

clue.text: They follow advice of Frenchman elevated in heels

indicators.note: the turned name goes inside the word for heels

parts.note: a ship heels or lists when it leans over

indicators.note: in a down clue, elevated means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: Rene is a typical French man's name

explanation.surface: Fans of advice who followed a Frenchman raised up in high heels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heels' looks like footwear but is the verb for a ship leaning; 'elevated' reads the name upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: People who listen to guidance heed it and act on it, so they follow advice.

clue.text: Savage opinion about uneven arse

indicators.note: the opinion word goes around the picked letters

parts.note: my bet is means my opinion is

indicators.note: the uneven, odd-numbered letters of the word are taken

explanation.surface: A crude verdict about someone's lopsided backside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uneven' picks the first and third letters of 'arse', A and S, which go inside BET.
explanation.definitionFit: A savage person or creature is a brute, so a beast.

clue.text: Dr 7, 9, 17 or 26 treated stars

indicators.note: treated means processed or worked on, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the two letters as written
these four answers are all anagrams of each other, so any supplies the same seven letters

explanation.surface: A doctor treats some celebrities.
explanation.walkthrough: TAGINES, GENISTA, EASTING and TEASING share their letters, so any of the four with DR is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Red giants are large cool stars late in their life, swollen and reddish.

clue.text: Plant one well-versed in service at front of church

indicators.note: this places the first piece before the second in the answer

parts.note: a vet, short for veteran, is someone with long experience of military service

explanation.surface: A seasoned old soldier stands at the front of a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: Vetch is a leguminous climbing plant grown as fodder and green manure.

clue.text: Facetiously puts one — and others like it — in order

definitions.text: Facetiously puts one — and others like it — in order

parts.words: Facetiously puts one — and others like it — in order
parts.note: the word facetiously contains the five letters a, e, i, o and u, each once and in alphabetical order

explanation.surface: Someone jokingly lines up a thing and its companions.
explanation.definitionFit: Each of a, e, i, o and u is a speech sound letter of this kind, and facetiously holds them all in sequence.

clue.text: Having silver forks, partly eating stews

indicators.note: the forks' prongs take in the silver, eating it

parts.note: tines are the prongs, part of a fork
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Dining with the silver cutlery, part-way through eating some stews.
explanation.definitionFit: Tagines are slow-cooked North African stews, named after the pot they are cooked in.

clue.text: Uncompromising, aggressive advertising that's hard to stop

indicators.note: the letter plugs or stops the gap in the middle of the phrase

parts.note: a hard sell is a pushy sales approach
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Pushy marketing that is difficult to halt.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard-shell position is rigid and unyielding, like a hard-shell Baptist's strict views.

clue.text: Low-down volunteers holding one's broom

indicators.note: the outer pieces hold the next piece inside them

parts.note: gen is British slang for the inside information, the low-down
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force
one's read as one is gives I plus S

explanation.surface: Inside information about volunteer soldiers keeping hold of someone's sweeping brush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broom' is the shrub, not the brush the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Genista is the botanical genus of broom, a yellow-flowered shrub.

clue.text: Old girl wants silver included in endowment

indicators.note: the second piece goes inside the first one

parts.note: a dower is the property given to a widow or an endowment
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: An elderly woman expects her silver to be part of her settlement.
explanation.definitionFit: A dowager is a widow holding a title from her late husband, often an imposing elderly lady.

clue.text: Concise section of chapter seven

indicators.note: section of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An editor praising one brief part of a book's seventh chapter.
explanation.definitionFit: Terse means brief and to the point, using few words.

clue.text: Transport found in slip roads

parts.note: to trip is to slip or stumble
lanes are narrow roads

explanation.surface: Means of getting about discovered on motorway slip roads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' is a link, not a container signal; 'Transport' means aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: Triplanes are aircraft with three sets of wings, so a form of transport.

clue.text: Voice of wheelwright?

parts.note: a wheelwright, read whimsically, is a man of spokes, and a voice for a group is its official speaker

explanation.surface: Who speaks for the trade of wheel-makers?
explanation.definitionFit: A person who speaks on behalf of others is their voice, and a wheelwright works with the spokes of wheels.

clue.text: Has caged cattle on board, trembling

indicators.note: being on board means being inside the steamship letters

parts.note: on board means aboard a ship, SS being a steamship

indicators.note: the cattle are caged inside the word has

parts.note: kine is an old plural of cow, meaning cattle

explanation.surface: A ship carrying caged livestock rocks as it goes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' is the crossword convention for going inside the steamship letters, after 'caged' puts the cattle inside 'Has'.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakiness is a state of trembling or unsteadiness.

clue.text: Spanish woman has Spanish man in grass

indicators.note: the woman has the man inside her name

parts.note: Maria is a common Spanish woman's name
Juan is a common Spanish man's name

explanation.surface: A Spanish couple lying together in a meadow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in grass' looks like part of the scene, but 'grass' is slang for cannabis.
explanation.definitionFit: Grass is slang for cannabis, the drug smoked as a joint.

clue.text: HQ quashing end of wildcat strike

indicators.note: the first piece squashes down on and encloses the second

parts.note: a base is a headquarters

indicators.note: only the last letter of the following word is used

explanation.surface: Headquarters cracks down on an unofficial walk-out by workers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wildcat strike' is a sudden unofficial stoppage, but 'strike' is the definition, meaning beat.
explanation.definitionFit: To baste someone is an old word for thrashing them, so to strike or beat.

clue.text: Programme made by outspoken actors

parts.note: broad speech is plain and outspoken
a cast is the set of actors in a production

explanation.surface: A show put together by actors who speak their minds.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadcast is a radio or television programme.

clue.text: Assists dealer, say, as stakes come in

indicators.note: the stakes word comes into the middle of the two-letter word

parts.note: a bet is a stake put on an outcome

explanation.surface: Someone helping a card dealer as the gamblers' money is laid on the table.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is fuller than 'Assists': to abet is to help a wrongdoer, and a drug dealer is one such.
explanation.definitionFit: Abetting is aiding someone in crime, as in aiding and abetting, so helping a criminal such as a pusher.

clue.text: Buffet fnally served in relaxing oriental course?

indicators.note: the letter is served up inside the word for relaxing

parts.note: easing means relaxing or loosening

indicators.note: only the last letter of the previous word is taken

explanation.surface: A buffet is laid on at the end of a soothing Asian meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course' looks like part of a meal but means a direction; 'fnally' is printed so.
explanation.definitionFit: An easting is a distance or course travelled eastward, so heading toward the Orient.

clue.text: Hours slip away for old unionist?

indicators.note: slipping away suggests the letters scattering into a new order

parts.note: taken as written as anagram material
taken as written as anagram material

explanation.surface: Time passes for an elderly trade-union man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unionist' suggests a trade unionist or Ulster unionist; here it is a fan of the old Soviet Union.
explanation.definitionFit: A Russophil admires Russia, and so might be a supporter of the former Soviet Union.

clue.text: Central characters in The Fifth Element

wordplay.reading: H and F, the middles of THE and FIFTH

parts.note: the middle letter of each word gives the two-letter chemical symbol Hf

explanation.surface: The main characters of the science-fiction film The Fifth Element.
explanation.walkthrough: The film title is a decoy: the middles of THE and FIFTH give Hf, the chemical symbol for this metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Hafnium is a chemical element, a metal with atomic number 72 and symbol Hf.

clue.text: Doing time post criminal activity

parts.note: someone doing time is inside, in prison
a post is a job

explanation.surface: Serving a sentence after committing a crime.
explanation.definitionFit: An inside job is a crime committed by or with help from someone within the organisation.

clue.text: Team race

definitions.meaning: ... County is an English football club
the Epsom horse race for three-year-olds

explanation.walkthrough: Derby County is a football club; the Derby is a famous flat race at Epsom in England.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to an English football club and to a celebrated horse-racing classic.

clue.text: Mad about European moderates

indicators.note: the word for mad goes around the letter

parts.note: bats is slang for crazy

explanation.surface: A crazy person complains about European centrists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moderates' looks like a noun for centrists; it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To bate is to lessen or restrain, as in with bated breath, so it moderates.

clue.text: He wrote in edge of notes off and on

indicators.note: every other letter is taken, skipping one and keeping the next

explanation.surface: Someone scribbled in the margin of the notes now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: Daniel Defoe was the English author of Robinson Crusoe, so a man who wrote.

clue.text: Prod mine and proceed!

parts.note: egg is old military slang for a bomb or mine
on! is a command to go forward

explanation.surface: A miner is urged to push forward.
explanation.definitionFit: To egg someone on is to urge or goad them, a verbal prod.

clue.text: State prisoner I treated on the inside

indicators.note: the answer lies within the letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A guard boasting about how he treated a prisoner while in jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the inside' suggests prison, but it signals the letters hidden inside the words.
explanation.definitionFit: Eritrea is a country in the Horn of Africa, a sovereign state.

clue.text: Drinks in gallons — that's worrying

parts.note: teas are drinks
taken as written

explanation.surface: Drinking by the gallon is cause for concern.
explanation.definitionFit: Teasing is pestering or annoying someone, so worrying them as a dog worries a bone.

clue.text: Inclined to yield, rugged husband's gone

indicators.note: the husband's letter has gone, so it is taken out

parts.note: shaggy means rough and rugged in appearance
H is the abbreviation for husband; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A rugged husband has left, perhaps ready to give in.
explanation.definitionFit: Something saggy droops and gives way under pressure, so it tends to yield.

clue.text: Touch wood, I'm no 4, 15 across, 16, 22 criminal

indicators.note: something criminal is bent or crooked, so the letters are twisted

parts.note: these letters are taken as written, without the apostrophe
these four answers are all made of the same five letters

explanation.surface: A superstitious person insists they are not one of those wrongdoers.
explanation.walkthrough: BEAST, BASTE, ABETS and BATES are all anagrams of one another, so any of them supplies the five letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Absit omen is Latin for may the omen be absent, said to ward off bad luck like touching wood.
